You are the one judge of an evidence rule for a children's maths game. Be strict and check by running things yourself. You cannot write files in the repository; return your whole verdict as your final message. You did not build this.

**The checkout to read and run:** <checkout at 46782fd15> (a read-only copy of the repository at the commit under judgement; run node from that directory; do not edit, commit or delete anything in it; write any scratch file of your own under <scratch>/judge-games8/work-kon-place/ only).

**What is being decided.** The game mode `kon/place` (class 6: placing a protractor and reading or drawing an angle (mix-ups: vertex-off, centre-on-arm, wrong-scale, join-wrong-end)) is already shown to children. It records right or wrong, first try or not, and the number of checks. It does NOT yet tell the teacher or the learner model that a child holds a particular mix-up ("naming"). Naming is switched on only if this evidence rule passes. The harm to prevent: a child who does NOT hold the mix-up being recorded as holding it, because of a blind guess, an ordinary slip, or a habit that has nothing to do with the mix-up.

**The law.** Over the levels of one sitting on which naming can happen (the session's first four), the chance that a child who does not hold the mix-up is named must be under 1 in 10.

**History.** A first reading on 2026-11-16 failed this mode: the proofs modelled a blind guess and one slip on independent levels, and a child with a habit (the same number, the same slip, the same order on every level) was named far too often. The ruling that followed made the proof a battery of "habit children" run through whole sessions as the server serves them, and then a second ruling added that a sighting counts only on a level where the mix-up and every habit child predict different acts. Games has built both. Read:
1. <checkout at 46782fd15>/docs/design/round8/games-judging/RULINGS-2026-11-16-gate2.md (H1 to H7; the list of children under H2).
2. <checkout at 46782fd15>/docs/design/round8/games-judging/RULINGS-2026-11-16-gate2-answers.md (the discriminating level; the level mix).
3. The packet: <checkout at 46782fd15>/docs/design/round8/games-judging/kon-place/PACKET.md, the sections "Gate 2: evidence" and "Gate 2 battery".
4. The battery: <checkout at 46782fd15>/tests/_habit-children.mjs and <checkout at 46782fd15>/tests/r8-habit-battery-kon-place.test.mjs. The rule as the server applies it: <checkout at 46782fd15>/server/play/levels.js, <checkout at 46782fd15>/shared/play.ts, <checkout at 46782fd15>/src/play/core/replay.ts and <checkout at 46782fd15>/src/play/families/kon/kon.logic.ts and src/play/families/kon/kon.place.ts.
5. The first reading's verdict for this mode, for what was found then: <checkout at 46782fd15>/docs/design/round8/games-judging/kon-place/judges/gate2-judge-2026-11-16.md.

**Your one question: is a child missing from the battery?** That is, is there a child a class-4-to-6 teacher would recognise, who does not hold the mix-up, whom this rule names in 1 session in 10 or more? Do it this way:

Confirm it passes and that its negative control (the same children under the old rules) still shows the old failures. Give the worst non-holder figure you see, by goal.
B. **List the children it has**, by goal, in one line each.
C. **Think of the children it lacks.** Work from the game's acts as a child meets them on a phone: every way of answering that does not come from the mix-up but is consistent from level to level or follows from the screen. Consider at least: the same wrong act every level; an act copied from the last level (right or wrong, hers or the play-out's); always the first, last, middle, nearest, largest or smallest option; reading across the screen in each direction; a finger that lands a fixed distance from its target in any direction; a child who answers at random after a miss; a child who does the solve she was just shown on the next level whatever it asks; a child who alternates; a child who types the number printed nearest the answer box; a careful child with two slips in a session; a child who holds a DIFFERENT mix-up of the same mode. For each candidate not already in the battery, write it as a child (a few lines using the tool's own helpers, in a scratch file under your work folder that imports from <checkout at 46782fd15>/tests/_habit-children.mjs) and run it through served sessions at every fade.
